text:
Marco Rossi arrived in Vancouver in the December 2025 trade that sent Quinn Hughes to Minnesota, so every stretch of his gets read as a verdict on that deal. This one is hard going. He has 7 points in 19 games and no goals in his last ten, and his ice time over that stretch is down two and a half minutes a night, to 14.25.

The results are lagging the work. His three goals sit right on 3.29 expected goals (the quality of his chances), his points rate (1.43 per 60) is below the bottom of our talent range for him, and Vancouver has scored 3.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis caught one example Friday: "a tough break for the #Canucks after a strong shift by the Rossi line." Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.6 wins above replacement last season, much of it on the power play, with teammates in the bottom 8%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 70% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Those are a useful center's skills on a team that has lost nine of ten.
headline: Marco Rossi's minutes slip while the work goes on
